utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in court today. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And may we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Aditya Menon for the Prosecution, assisted by our case managers, Alma Imamovic and Fraser McIlwraith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to my learned friends from the OTP, everyone in and around this courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson on behalf of General Rasim Delic, joined here today by our case manager, Lejla Gluhic, and our case manager Lana Deljkic, as well as Asja Zujo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Sir, yesterday, before you started your testimony, you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to remind you that you are still bound by that declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, PW-9.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Last evening when we broke, we were talking about Mehmed Jusic, and I had asked you a question, as reflected on lines 12 through 16 of page 5571 concerning Mr. Jusic, and you said: "Jusic had a serious injury of the face and eye, and it was the practice in the El Mujahedin Detachment that the wounded who could not properly be treated in Bosnia be treated abroad, and their treatment would be paid for." Do you remember saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, PW-9, who arranged the requisite travel documents for these El Mujahedin Detachment members so that they could travel abroad for such medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. That was not the sort of job that I was involved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you know, sir, whether anyone other than Mr. Jusic from the El Mujahedin Detachment received medical treatment abroad?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that Residik Djazari [phoen] travelled with him to Malaysia and later on to Freiburg.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would ask that PT1882 be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 1882, thank you very much. PT1882 is marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, MFI 832.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-9, in your written statement, at paragraphs 277 and 278, you describe a farewell ceremony for the El Mujahedin Detachment. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, sir, the date and location of this farewell ceremony, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was the 1st of January, 1996, and the place was the Army Home in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, approximately how many people attended this ceremony?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several hundred people, probably between 200 and 300, perhaps even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall, sir, the identity or names of any of the persons who attended that ceremony?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember many persons, many names. Do you want to know about anything in particular -- anyone in particular?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir, if there were any senior military leaders present.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. General Rasim Delic was there, the 3rd Corps Commander Sakib Mahmuljin was there. The Commander of the 35th Division, Fadil Hasanagic, and a number of other officers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about senior members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.; do you recall if any of those persons were present, and if so, can you tell us who?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Abu Maali, the Commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall anyone else that might be considered among the leadership of the El Mujahedin Detachment who was present?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muris Supic. I was there, too. And others who might be considered to have been among the leadership were not there. In recent events, most of those who belonged to the detachment's command were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What do you mean, sir, as least in the English when it says, "In recent events, most of those who belonged to the detachment's command were killed"; what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the events that immediately preceded the farewell ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say "most of those who belonged to the detachment's command were killed," to whom are you referring?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above all, Sheik Enver Saban, Muatez Masri, Nedzdi, Abu Zijad, Muhariz Libi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think the recorder has been left behind because of the difficulty with the names, spellings I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's take them one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You mentioned, sir, Sheik Enver Saban. Do you recall approximately when Sheik Enver Saban was killed?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in mid-November, but I'm not certain. I'm talking about 1995, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I also heard you say "Muatez," sir, and that's not reflected in the transcript. Was Mr. Muatez killed before this farewell ceremony on 1 January 1996, and if so, do you recall approximately when?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Muatez was killed on the 22nd of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, other than Saban and Muatez, there's some question in the transcript, the names of the other individuals that you mentioned who had been killed prior to the 1 January 1996 farewell ceremony?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also mentioned Nedzdi, Abu Zijad, and Abu Haris Libi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when Abu Haris Libi was killed?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Together with Sheik Enver Saban. He and Abu Nedzdi, they were killed together with Sheik Enver Saban.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's return to this farewell ceremony. Can you tell us what happened at that ceremony, what transpired at that ceremony?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the ceremony itself, several speeches were given; many, in fact. There was also some entertainment, songs and dance, that sort of thing. That's all I can say, in general terms. Perhaps I could provide further details, if requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, PW-9, who made speeches at the farewell ceremony on 1 January 1996?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that Abu Maali spoke, the Commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Another person who spoke was General Rasim Delic. Also, the 3rd Corps Commander, Sakib Mahmuljin, Abdu Melicbasic, Ahmed Adilovic, Sefik Kurdic, and there might have been other speakers, too. There were quite a number of speeches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, with respect to the speech given by General Rasim Delic, if there was anyone who interpreted his comments into the Arabic language?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two interpreters who were interpreting the speeches. One was Iman Howad [as interpreted] and the other was Abdulmelik Basic. [Realtime transcript read in error "Halid Basic"]. I'm not sure who interpreted for which particular speaker. I can't remember with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, sir, I think the transcript has failed to capture the names of these two persons. Can you repeat who it was that were doing the interpreting?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ajman Awad and Abdulmelik Basic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-9, to the best of your recollection, sir, can you tell us what you remember General Rasim Delic saying at this farewell ceremony on 1 January 1996 in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, General Delic conveyed the greetings of President Izetbegovic. He briefly thanked the Arabs for their assistance to the Bosnian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you be more specific of what you remember him saying?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe General Delic also said he believed that in case of need, he would be able to count on the assistance of the Arab peoples, again that the Arab peoples would indeed again be fully prepared to grant their assistance to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember if General Delic made any specific comments about the effectiveness of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember anything like that being said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir, because in paragraph 278 of your written statement, it's written, in the middle of that paragraph: "Rasim Delic was thankful because the El Mujahid Detachment was one of the best units in the entire ABiH." Do you remember writing that in your statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that as being part of my statement. It is quite possible that this was, in fact, said. It's possible. I can't be positive about it. It may have been Rasim Delic or perhaps another speaker who spoke on the occasion, but I can't say with absolute certainty who was it that uttered the actual words.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time we would ask that PT6199 be shown to the witness, to include both the video and audio components thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, PW-9, I'm going to show you now a tape, and I would like you to look very carefully at it and listen very carefully to the tape. And once the tape is finished, I'm going to ask you to comment upon the tape and ask you perhaps some follow-up questions concerning the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Farewell ceremony of Mujahid 4. General Sakib Mahmuljin's speech or address. The address of Army General of the Republic of B and H, Rasim Delic. That's what our representatives once said, and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-9, could you comment on what you just observed and heard on this videotape?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to say that the image that I could see is not consistent with the atmosphere that prevailed at this farewell ceremony that I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I mean is this: We were actually indoors, and this is an outdoor venue. You can see that clearly in the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With respect, sir, then, to the audio component of this tape, can you comment upon what you heard on this tape?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is reference in the tape of these being the speeches given by General Mahmuljin and General Delic. The voices do sound a bit like their voices, but I can in no way be positive about the fact that those were indeed their voices.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about the contents of what was said, sir; can you comment upon the contents of what was said on the tape?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that General Delic conveyed the president's greetings and that he thanked the Arabs. However, I do not remember the portions where he speaks about his meeting with NATO and the command-and-control system. I am not familiar with that. I don't think he would have been likely to address issues of this nature at a ceremony of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, did you recognise the voice of the person speaking in Arabic on the tape?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sounds like the voice of Ajman Awad, but again I can't be positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would ask that this tape be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The tape is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 833.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just one moment, please, Your Honours. I would ask that the witness now be shown the document marked PT1540.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps while that's coming up, PW-9, let me ask you this question: In your statement at paragraph 40, you made reference to a place called Dzotlina Kuca. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you recall about this location and the El Mujahedin Detachment at that place?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This action took place just before I joined the El Mujahedin Detachment. I didn't personally witness this. The operation was a fresh one, so to speak, so I heard a number of references to that operation and I did see some recordings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say, "I heard a number of references to that operation and I did see some recordings," can you tell us what you were told or what you saw on these recordings concerning this location and any operations that occurred there?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I heard was that it was an operation of the El Mujahedin Detachment on the HVO line at Dzotlina Kuca, that a unit was smashed there, a sabotage platoon, the so-called Jokers, and in the footage I saw scenes from the fighting and the fortifications on the HVO line. This is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And other than the El Mujahedin Detachment, sir, do you recall whether you were told or saw on this videotape the involvement of any other military units of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw were just members of the El Mujahedin Detachment. I didn't see members from other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the document on the screen in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please scroll to the very bottom part of the Bosnian language and go to page 2 of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-9, I would draw your attention to the very last paragraph in the Bosnian version, and it would be the second paragraph in English under the heading "Our Forces."

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you comment upon that paragraph, in light of what you were told or what you observed on the recordings shortly after you joined the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that some other units are being mentioned in coordinated action with the El Mujahedin Detachment, but it's not really a fact that this happened. And the rest is the way I already stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to the admission of this document. The witness said that he didn't know anything about the participation of the units mentioned in the document. The witness did not participate in the action. He just said that he saw video footage from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The Prosecution would also draw the Chamber's attention to paragraph 40 of the witness's written statement, where he indicated the same information, that he'd heard about this operation and had seen video recordings about it, and this document certainly relates to what the witness was told and what the witness observed on the videotape. And that, we would submit, is a proper foundational basis for the document being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm on my feet. It's true, what the witness said does have something to do with it. He said he heard of the Dzotlina Kuca action. He saw the footage, heard about it. However, he did not see -- he's not an eyewitness of the events relating to the facts that are mentioned here, the participation of the units, as mentioned in the document. For each document, we could find some connection between the witness and the document, but specifically here, units are mentioned here that the witness said he knows nothing about. So I think that no basis or grounds have been established for the admission of this document on the basis of the knowledge of this witness. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 834.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution would ask that the witness now be shown the document marked PT1566, 1566.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness PW-9, I would ask you to take a look at this document, and then I'm going to ask you if you can shed any light on the information that's set forth in this document, please.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that this is a report on the death of four members of the El Mujahedin Detachment and the capture of one member. This also happened before I came to the detachment. I was present when the bodies were exchanged and when those who were killed were buried near the village of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us who these four members of the El Mujahedin Detachment that were killed were? Do you know the identities of these four persons that were killed, as reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For one, I know that that was Wahiddin Masri, and I think another one was called "Abu Hamza." The rest or the others, I don't know, I'm really not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say "Abu Hamza," do you know which Abu Hamza was killed on this day?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Abu Hamza, there were really many of them. I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And there's also a reference in this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just find out something. Were there many Abu Hamzas in the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were many.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps before I continue, PW-9, do you recall whether -- how did you distinguish between these different Abu Hamzas?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were from different countries. One was Abu Hamza Masri from Egypt, another one was Abu Hamza Suri from Syria, another one was Abu Hamza Tunis from Tunisia, so that was the way. They also had some additional nicknames, and that's how we could tell them apart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And are you not able to tell whether this Abu Hamza who died, whether he was a Masri or Syria or Tunisia? [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I really couldn't say. I never met those people. I was just present when the bodies were exchanged and at their funeral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, among the leadership of the El Mujahedin Detachment, were any of the leaders known as "Abu Hamza"?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only Abu Hamza that had some sort of function at the detachment was Abu Hamza Muhadzir, who was the head of the detachment's press centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, perhaps if we could, Your Honour, just briefly go into private session, if we could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, there is undeniably a link to the witness between -- this document and the witness, but what is the relevance?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It goes, Your Honours, to the issue of the death of Commander Wahiddin, who has obviously been mentioned numerous times in the course of this trial, and puts a definitive date on the time period in which that individual was killed, among other issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This does not appear to be coming out of the document, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first line indicates "In the Novi Travnik area on 2 October 1993, four BH army members from the El Mujahedin unit were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I can see that, but is Commander Wahiddin's name mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, but the witness just testified that he was one of the persons. I can find that for you in the transcript. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Should we go into private session for this discussion? It looks like we're going back to this document which we discussed in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the only reason we discussed this in private session was with respect to the wounded person. There is no other reason. This document does not necessarily need to be under seal because it doesn't identify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I understand, but from Judge Harhoff's questions, it looks like we're going back, and maybe just for the sake of safety, let's go back into private session. [Private session].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown PT1776, PT1776.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-9, do you see the document on the screen in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we be assisted to determine the date of the document? The English doesn't show the year. It says the year is illegible. Is anybody able to read the year on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see, in paragraph 2 of this document, reference to a date? Perhaps that can assist us with respect to the date of the document.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the date, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the date of the document is, if you're able to do that, PW-9?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date of the document is the 2nd of August, 1994, it seems, and then in the second paragraph of the order it says "the 15th of August, 1994".

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the reference in the second paragraph is to what date, sir? What is to happen by the 15th of August, 1994?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order to relocate the El Mujahedin Detachment from Mehurici to the Trokuce-Zenica facility by the 19th of August, 1994, at the latest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps there's been an interpretation error. Sir, did you say this was to be accomplished by the 19th of August, 1994, this move?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said by the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, sir, what this Trokuce-Zenica facility refers to? What is that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the Vatrostalna facility that is in Trokuce. It's a neighbourhood in the town of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know the area known as Podbrezje near Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, where Podbrezje is in relation to Trokuce?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two neighbourhoods, one next to the other, actually. Vatrostalna was on the border between Podbrezje and Trokuce.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what was this Vatrostalna facility in August 1994, what was in that building or location?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vatrostalna was the barracks of the El Mujahedin Detachment, but that was a barracks already from the time that I came to the detachment, from October 1993. I don't know whether the El Mujahedin Detachment was already there before, but when I got there, the El Mujahedin Detachment had already taken up that -- the barracks. The detachment was there from January 1994. That was the main barracks of the detachment from that time, so I don't really see the sense of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what is the reference to Mehurici in this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Poljanica, near Mehurici, the detachment also had its barracks. We called it "the Mehurici barracks."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, once again I object to the admission of this document. The witness has just said that he does not see the sense in this order, and I don't see how the witness could be linked with this. He said the Command of El Mujahid was already there in October 1993 at Vatrostalna, so the witness did not confirm anything that is contained in this document in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness, based on his statement, was a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment. He's told us what the Vatrostalna facility is. This document clearly does not purport to establish any kind of facility in Trokuce-Zenica, but simply talks about relocating from one area to another, and the witness has clearly laid the foundation for this document to go into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 836.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the transcript, I would like to state that I'm very concerned with the different standard of admission of documents. Two days ago, we had a situation with a document that had to do with -- or that the Trial Chamber refused to admit in relation to the witness Zilkic. Also, it was evident that the witness was talking about the same contents. The situation was identical. I'm very concerned that the standard changes. We had one standard in that case, and today we have a different standard. I would like this to be recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you for your observations, Mrs. Vidovic. I think the core of the matter here is that the decisions to admit or not to admit documents into evidence are very frequently decisions that take some discretion, and the Bench is trying at all times to ensure that the documents that do come into evidence and are admitted through a witness do so because there is a sufficient link between the witness and the document. I admit that in the last two examples here, the link seems to be not very obvious, but nevertheless we did find that in the first case, in the first document, the fact that the witness had mentioned a particular battle in his statement and was shown the video-recordings of it would establish a sufficient link. And for this last document, we think that the fact that he was a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment and knew of both places also constitutes a link, not very obvious, but nevertheless, as I said, it's a discretionary decision and we think that although it may not be very clear, we think that there was a sufficient link. And so it's not a question of having a different standard from one day to the next. You always have to consider that the decisions can be difficult to make, but we are trying to have as clear practice as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just say to you, Madam Vidovic, also that you realise that in addition to what Judge Harhoff has said, we also make decisions based on what the parties tell us. Now, you objected to this document on the basis that the witness has just said that he does not see the sense in this order. Now, I have not known of making sense of a document being a basis for admission or not admission of a document. He doesn't have to agree with what is written in the document. He doesn't have to -- he's told us what he has told us to establish the link, and you have not said that he didn't -- the link was not established. You just told us that he had said he sees no sense, that he doesn't -- you don't see how the witness could be linked with this. He said the Commander of the El Mujahid was already there in October 1993. We don't know whether it was there in 1993 already, and we don't know what went into the mind of the person who made the order after 1993. However, he has told -- just explained it to us. Making sense goes to the question of probative value, not to the question of admission. Yes, Mr. Mundis. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I thought that I was quite clear and that I had said that I did not see any link between this witness and the document. I think that I was clear. The witness did mention the event, but that is why I specifically mentioned the example with Witness Zilkic, where it was clear that throughout his testimony the witness did mention the event, which you will recall was in the document, one of the last documents that had to do with Zilkic's credibility. The entire time, that witness talked about that event, but then it was said that the witness does not accept the document. Now we have had the same situation. I think that I was clear. First of all, he had nothing to do with the document. Secondly, it's clear from the witness's testimony is that he does not accept that document as correct, and this is what I saw there to indicate that there is no link or connection between the document and the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I want to stay clear of discussing the Zilkic matter because I don't have a recollection of the incident you're referring to, so I will not comment on that. It is safe to say when you say, "But then it was said that the witness does not accept the document," I'm not quite sure whether you can refer us to a quotation in the transcript about that with the Zilkic matter. Situations where a witness has spoken about the contents of the matter, and we did not admit those documents, I remember two, one on the side of the Defence, another on the side of the Prosecution, where the witness clearly denied knowledge of what was written on the document, and on both of those occasions, the Bench said what the parties are doing are establishing a link between the document and some other incident, but not between the witness and the document. And I can't remember the witnesses, but I have no recollection of the Zilkic matter, unless you want to take us back to that one, but I think we're dealing with this objection. We have ruled on this objection, and I think the matter can rest at that point. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd ask that the witness now be shown PT1791. PT1791.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, sir: In paragraph 75 of your statement, you make reference to Visoka Glava and Pisana Jelika. Can you tell us about those places and what you were talking about in paragraph 75 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Visoka Glava and Pisana Jelika, those are facilities at the Serici-Teslic theatre of war which the El Mujahedin Detachment took in one of its actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This a decision by the Commander of the 3rd Corps to attack, to launch an attack. I'd never seen the document before it was shown to me by the OTP. In paragraph 3.2, I see a reference there to the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. If we could go to the next page, please, in the English version to paragraph 3.2. It's in the bottom half of page 2. In the English, it's towards the bottom of the page, in the Bosnian original, paragraph 3.2 -- Yes, sir, sorry to interrupt. Can you comment upon what's said in paragraph 3.2 of this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that the El Mujahedin Detachment was supposed to attack the following facilities: Pisana Jelika and Visoka Glava. All I can say is that the El Mujahedin Detachment completed this action --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir --

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Sometime in the summer of 1994. I think in late July or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could see the date of this document. If we could scroll to the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the date of this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the date, I see it. I thought it was sometime earlier on, but it's quite possible that it was in late August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, PW-9, what involvement, if any, you personally had in respect of this operation?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was personally involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How so and at what place, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I led one of the groups at Visoka Glava.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, PW-9, from whom did you receive your orders to take your group to Visoka Glava?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received my orders from Muatez. He was the detachment's deputy commander for military issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we do so, I would like the witness to be shown again part 3.2 of the document, and my question is: How was this order made? Witness, you told us that it was issued by the Commander of the 3rd Corps, Mr. Mahmuljin, and yet you also told us that your orders were given by Muatez, so I'm curious to know on which basis did General Mahmuljin issue the order here, do you know, and were you involved in the making of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already said I'd never saw this order before I was shown the order by the OTP. I do not know that the 3rd Corps commander issued this order. Likewise, I don't know that some of the units mentioned here in the document were, in fact, involved in the operation. I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I thought you said, but maybe I was -- maybe I'm wrong, I thought you said that this is an order issued by the Commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just read what the document actually says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, sir, when you went into combat, did your platoon or your unit work together with other units of the 3rd Corps, not being part of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, only the El Mujahedin Detachment was involved in this operation, no one else. The nature of this particular mission, the lie of the land and the way the facilities were, Visoka Glava and Pisana Jelika, were such that an operation could be conducted in terms of attacking these two features, quite regardless of any other features.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Perhaps we cannot squeeze more juice out of this apple, but I am curious to know if we can, at some point during this examination, during the examination of this witness, get a little closer to the way in which the combat operations were planned between the El Mujahid Detachment and the 3rd Corps. And since the witness might have been involved in the planning of such operations, I would be curious to hear his testimony thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'll ask the witness that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to this operation concerning the locations Pisana Jelika and Visoka Glava, what involvement, if any, did you have in planning that operation?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Day 1, when we reconnoitered these facilities, to the day the operation actually took place, I remained involved throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you describe for us how this planning took place, who was involved in the planning, where the planning occurred?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this was happening along the front line itself. Also involved, alongside with me, of course, were Muatez, who was assistant commander for military issues, as well as some other members of the detachment, Amir Puric, Abdulah Libi, Samadin Masri. We independently reconnoitered first and then carried out the actual operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, were you involved in any meetings or discussions with respect to the planning of this operation that involved anyone who was not a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. Leading question. The witness said they were independent, they planned the operation on their own, and now this suggestion is being made that there was a meeting attended by the persons who were not members of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness said that they independently reconnoitered first. That does not necessarily mean that they independently carried out the operation. And I don't believe that was a leading question. The question simply goes to the issue -- he's told us about planning happening all along the front line. He described to us persons who were involved in that planning. And my question was simply whether there was anyone who was not a member of the detachment who was involved in that planning, to his knowledge, were there any instance that he personally is aware of, and that's all I'm concerned with is his personal knowledge or personal involvement, whereby anyone from outside the detachment was involved in planning. If he doesn't know, he doesn't know. That's as far as we can take it, but I don't believe the question was leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-9, do you understand what I'm asking you, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand your question. No one else outside the El Mujahedin Detachment was involved in the planning of this operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question, Witness. The plan that the El Mujahedin Detachment prepared independently, was it approved by the units that were hierarchically above the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once the operation had been planned, the Command or the Commander of Operations Group 3 North was informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I would like to know who is Operations Group 3 North.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Operations Group 3 North was commanded by Colonel, I think, Jusuf Musinbegovic. This operations group included a number of units who were covering that area, and that was their area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This Operations Group 3 North, what army did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was part of the 3rd Corps of BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And it was not part of the El Mujahedin Detachment, either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, of course it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Okay, then -- sorry. Did you want to ask?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't quite understand. So it was at a higher level than the level of El Mujahid Detachment, this Operational Group 3 North, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right, that was a higher level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 837.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would that be a convenient time, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It would indeed, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we come back to the question raised by the Defence regarding the document that was not admitted on the 13th of November when it was submitted to Witness Zilkic. Madam Vidovic made a comparison with today's situation regarding the admission of the document. I just want to underline that the Trial Chamber, during the break, had an opportunity to look at the transcript, and the Chamber is of the view that, after all, this is a different situation, especially so because, as was rightly reminded by Madam Vidovic today, back then on the 13th of November it was a question of testing the credibility of the witness through this document, and it appears very clearly, looking at the transcript. So when it comes to the future assessment by the Trial Chamber, there is no need to admit such a document, and the Trial Chamber has all the elements it needs, based on the transcript, in order to assess this point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-9, before the break we were talking about these operations at Pisana Jelika and Visoka Glava. Can you briefly tell us or tell the Trial Chamber what happened with respect to those features and your personal involvement with your unit at those locations?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early that morning, and I can't remember the exact date, there were several groups, I think a total of seven, from the El Mujahedin Detachment that carried out an attack on the following elevations: Visoka Glava and Pisana Jelika. Those positions were soon taken. There was little to no resistance by the enemy, and the entire operation took no longer than ten minutes. Later on, members of the detachment stayed at those positions. They did not pull out. They fortified those positions. They dug some trenches. They laid mines in front of the immediate area, that sort of thing. Members of the detachment remained at those positions until the operation that took place on the 3rd of October, and I'm here referring to the operation at a number of neighbouring elevations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown the document marked PT1801, 1801.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you just briefly tell us what this document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I've seen this document before. This seems to be a report on elements affecting combat morale in units of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please go to the bottom of the Bosnian version of this document or the original, and go to the bottom half of page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, approximately two-thirds of the way down in the Bosnian version, do you see the paragraph -- or about halfway down, two-thirds down, that talks about OG-3 North?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, again, in the English version it's approximately in the middle of the page, right about where the little magnifying glass is there. Can you take a quick read through that paragraph of this document to yourself, sir, and then I'd ask you to comment upon that, please.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment, sir, on particularly the last sentence of that paragraph and what's contained therein?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads here that the El Mujahedin Detachment successfully took control of the features Pisana Jelika and Visoka Glava. I was not aware of the fact that all the other units mentioned in the report were also involved in any sort of offensive action on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But with respect to your unit, sir, what can you tell us about what's contained in this document with respect to your unit and the locations mentioned?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is mentioned here is precisely what I said in reply to one of your earlier questions about the taking of these features, Pisana Jelika and Visoka Glava, by the El Mujahedin Detachment. This really happened, but I can't confirm the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us, if you know, what was the relationship in 1994, or in the summer of 1994, to be more specific, between Operation Group 3 North and the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The detachment carried out these operations in the area of responsibility of OG-3 North. There were several meetings that took place at the Command of OG-3 North, and these meeting were attended by members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if there was any relationship in terms of hierarchical relationship between OG-3 North and the El Mujahedin Detachment in the summer of 1994?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that there was a hierarchal relationship, as you term it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, just for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, can you please -- because we have some -- the original documents, of course, are in Bosnian. Can you please spell the word "North" in the Bosnian language, for the record?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: S-J-E-V-E-R, Sjever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit 838.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraph 81 of your written statement, there are references to the locations Kajen Sopot and Brdo and the location Kikica Brdo. Can you tell us, to the best of your recollection, what those locations -- what was going on at those locations, as indicated in paragraph 81 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kajen Sopot and Brdo were the following features that the El Mujahedin Detachment took in its next operation on the 3rd of October, 1994. Kikic is one of the hills nearby, the next hill, and it was taken that same day by members of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us where -- you mentioned the operation on the 3rd of October, 1994. Where were you on that day or during that immediate time period, the first few days of October 1994?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 3rd of October, I and all the other members of the El Mujahedin Detachment were involved in this operation. The task of my group, in particular, was to take Kajen Sopot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about that operation involving Kajen Sopot and your group?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The preparations had been afoot for about a month before the operation was launched. There was daily reconnaissance. We constructed a path through the woods in order to be able to pull out our wounded. On that day, as per usual, because this was the case in the El Mujahedin Detachment, at sometime like 4.00 in the morning or half past 4.00, an attack was eventually launched on these positions. The entire operation took about 40 minutes, and all the groups belonging to the El Mujahedin Detachment carried out their tasks, completed their tasks, which means that Kajen Sopot, Previja and Brdo were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask the witness now be shown PT1824.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wish to state for the record that this sort of examination should be conducted in keeping with Rule 92 ter. This is indeed quite distant from the instructions that the Chamber provided on examining 92 ter witnesses. This is a situation where we have an enormous witness statement that we are dealing with. At this point in time, I think we've been going on for about two and a half hours with this witness. One thing I wish you to know is that the established practice at this Tribunal is that the Defence is allotted four times as long as the OTP. This opens up a whole lot of issues that I have to prepare for. I don't think this the right way to go about this. We have pointed out time and again that this witness is no witness to be examined like this, that this would not be an appropriate 92 ter witness, in the expectation that something like this would take place. It really makes no sense. We have an enormous statement being tendered and exhibited, and then on top of that, we use up so much time to hear the witness live in this courtroom. I really have no idea why this should be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honours, I'm not aware -- I'm not aware of any established practice at this Tribunal that would permit the Defence to be allocated four times as long as the OTP. Second, excluding the statement of this witness, the Prosecution has shown this witness 15 documents. This is the 15th and final document or exhibit to be shown to the witness. This document, in particular, relates to paragraph 81 of the witness's statement. It is cited to in paragraph 29.1 of the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution. I have about two questions or three questions to ask this witness concerning this document, and that will be the end of the direct examination. I will also note that during the course of this witness's direct examination, there have been a number of interventions, which is completely within the rights of Madam Vidovic to make, but of course does consume additional time. I'm not faulting anyone for such interventions. I simply note that, of course, each and every intervention, such as this present one, means that there is less time available for us to focus on the evidence that the witness has to bear. Again, I don't think there's anything improper about showing a witness 15 documents or exhibits. That's certainly well within the established practice with respect to Rule 92 ter, and the Prosecution doesn't see anything at all improper or inappropriate with respect to this procedure. If Madam Vidovic requires additional time to cross-examine the witness, so be it. I'm not aware of anything, however, that would, as a standing rule, permit her four times as much time as the Prosecution takes. If she has eight or ten hours of relevant cross-examination, again, so be it, but to simply stand up and object as to the number of documents that we're showing, when it's a relatively small number of documents as in this case, I think is not perhaps the best use of the Trial Chamber's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to respond to both parties by saying the following, and let me start with what you are saying, Mr. Mundis. My understanding of the use of Rule 92 ter, 92 bis, is that the idea is to cut down on time; that the witness will say as much as he would have said viva voce in a written statement, and that when the witness comes into court, he just gets introduced, he's shown his statement, he confirms the statement, he states that that's the statement he would have given if he was led viva voce, and then the statement speaks for itself. I certainly find it a little out of step when a 92 ter or a 92 bis -- well, 92 bis is not even here -- a 92 ter witness is called, a lot of time is taken. I hear what you say, there have been a number of interventions and what have you. Be that as it may, I want to find out: Is it not possible for the witness, in his written statement, 92 ter statement, to refer to the exhibits that are going to be shown to say, "I've looked at those exhibits, I authenticate them," and they can be tendered, so that when his statement is tendered, it is tendered at least with those exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, at one point earlier, in September, I believe, and I can certainly find the filing, the Prosecution proposed doing just that, and we produced two 92 ter statements that had tables with such a description, and those witness statements were rejected by the Trial Chamber. We did do a similar exercise with respect to a witness last week, and the Chamber allowed us to tender a large number of exhibits through that witness on an exceptional basis. We are, of course, always open to anything that can expedite the proceedings. The express language of Rule 92 ter says that the witness's evidence may be heard in whole or in part by way of written evidence, and of course we would submit that that suggests a more expansive approach with respect to written statements. I believe had I taken this witness through all of the information and evidence contained in his written statement, that that would have taken us several days to accomplish, and to that extent I believe reducing that from several days of evidence to several hours of evidence certainly expedites the proceedings. The alternative approach, or one alternative approach, again, would be for us to link these documents by way of a Bar table motion after the witness appears and simply say, "This document relates to this paragraph of the witness's testimony." In light of the Chamber's previous rulings and guidelines concerning the requirement that we link a witness to -- or the documents to the witness's testimony has led us to this path that we are now -- in the most expeditious way possible, I'm trying to link the witness's written statement to certain documents. And again we're talking about 15 documents. This is the last one of which is now about to be called up onto the screen. And I do believe that we're moving as expeditiously as possible in order to focus in on what we've identified and what I've referred to here before as "the core exhibits," that is, exhibits that are cited to in our pre-trial brief, exhibits that the Prosecution believes are absolutely essential for the Trial Chamber to have before it in order for the Trial Chamber to make the ultimate decisions that fall within the responsibility of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Just two points I'm going to make. I hear what you say about the ruling that was made by the Chamber earlier, but I think we have always said, and I seem to remember that it was said by Judge Harhoff, that the Chamber does not mind a few documents being tendered with a statement, but when they become too many, that it becomes problematic. Now, the question is the definition of "few." Is 15 few or is it not few? It's a relative term. The other point is you have referred me and refreshed my memory about the wording of 92 ter, which says "may be heard in whole or in part," and on that basis I have no choice but to say: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown PT1824. 1824.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness PW-9, do you see this document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could zoom out and get the full page in both languages, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you briefly tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've not seen this document before. This is a report of the 3rd Corps Command, I believe, about assault actions in the area of responsibility of the 3rd North Group in October 1994. The El Mujahedin Detachment is mentioned in the first paragraph, saying that it has captured the facilities of Kajen Sopot, Previja and Brdo, and then it says something about the 319th Brigade which I believe is not correct. The El Mujahid Detachment actually quite independently carried out this assignment without the presence of any other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say "quite independently carried out this assignment," can you explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that in this operation, no member of any other unit participated. It was only members of the El Mujahedin Detachment who participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, you told us a few moments ago, I believe, that your group was involved with respect to this operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, which of these features did your group take on 3 October 1994?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the Kajen Sopot feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, if you recall, why your group took the Kajen Sopot feature or why your group went to this feature?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a continuation of previous operation, when Pisana Jelika and Visoka Glava were captured. The line was severed there, and the front line needed to be straightened out so that it would all go along one plane. Well, it's a bit hard for me to explain it now without a map. We received the order from Muatez. He's the deputy commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment for military affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would tender this document PT1824 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Just before we do that: Are you able to tell us, sir, who captured Previja and Brdo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Previja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, my poor language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Previja and Brdo were also captured by members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, why I was asking the question is because at page 40, line 10, you were asked a question: "And, sir, which of these features did your group take on 3 October 1994?" Now, of course, I don't know what is meant by "group" here, and you said: "That's the Kajen Sopot feature." Now, what did you mean by "group"? What did you understand by "group" when you were asked about a group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My group, where I was, and the group which I commanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Some unit within the El Mujahedin Detachment [Microphone not activated] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot hear the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My fault. When you say the group that you led, do you mean that you're talking about a small unit within a bigger El Mujahedin unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are there other groups that were not specifically led by you but also belonging to El Mujahedin who captured other groups.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry, it looks like my microphone keeps going off without me switching it off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we had tendered PT1824 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. PT1824 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 839.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, can we move to private session, please, now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When we are talking about this document that has to do with the certificates, you also saw that the payments were carried out by the Ministry of Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The Ministry of Defence made the payments via the Municipal Defence Secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would you agree that the Defence Ministry is a body of the government with us in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course it's a body of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I am now going to move to another topic. In paragraph 43 of your statement, you talked about the participation of the Mujahedin in combat actions in spring 1993, and you said that there was no operation close to their base in which they did not participate. In this connection, I would like to ask you the following: These were operations before the El Mujahedin Detachment was formed; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The detachment was officially formed on the 13th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You don't know at all if the people who, on the 13th of August joined the detachment took part in these combat actions; would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, I don't know. I was not an eyewitness of those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: From what I understood you to say, you came to Bosnia and Herzegovina only in September or October 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was the 27th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you could have only heard some stories that you cannot assert are correct, because you did not take part in these events?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I just heard something about those events. Of course, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Before the documents were shown to you by the OTP, you didn't see any documents from within the detachment that discuss these events?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, I did not see those documents or any documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we move back into private session at this point, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May somebody help us with the curtain, with the blind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please don't help us any longer. Thank you so much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It was because of these differences that they waged war on each other in their own respective areas of origin sometimes, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about those clashes, although I, myself, never travelled to any of those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What I have in mind is the following: Sunni Muslims came to Bosnia and Herzegovina, but also Shiite Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be put away, please. I want the witness to look at a different document now, P2216.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, here is another document produced by the Military Security Administration. The date is the 7th of July, 1995. This is about the activities carried out by members of the El Mujahid unit. "Information," it reads. It's a rather short document. I will quote you the portion that I'm interested in. It reads: "The State Security Service of the RBH, Ministry of the Interior, informed us that a source had told them that some members of the El Mujahid unit were talking about allegedly preparing an action to liquidate several members of the Shiite sect whose ideology and beliefs are propagated by Iranians and some of our own citizens, such as 'the hooting dervishes' from the territory of Travnik, whose names are known to some members of the El Mujahid unit." Witness, first of all, are you aware of the development described in this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this document in my life. I'm certain that the El Mujahid Detachment never planned the killing of any of these people, the Shiites or anyone else. Secondly, I'm sure this never materialised. Now, whether perhaps there were individuals who were members of the El Mujahedin Detachment who were planning this, obviously I can't be certain either way. Again, I've never seen this document before. I do have to point out that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, the Iranians, the Shiites, were not members of the detachment, there was a certain amount of mutual repulsion, if I may call it that. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not a single Shiite who was a member of the El Mujahid Detachment. Needless to say, if I may just add to my answer, it would have been impossible precisely because of these ideological differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that in Central Bosnia, in 1993, 1994 and 1995, there were such groups as well?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were all sorts of groups there, Afro-Asians -- there were a lot of groups that existed in the area at the time, in addition to the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Existed and, in fact, fought there in 1994 and 1995; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said "groups," I meant groups that were involved in the actual fighting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, may the document be exhibited, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do so, just for my own edification, what are "hooting dervishes"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the way it's written here is a little clumsy. There were dervishes, the hooting dervishes. "Hooting" is slightly derogatory, I think. "Dervishes," on the other hand, they are a group among Muslims who espouse a Sufi philosophy. I think this would require a lengthy explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We don't need a lengthy one. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 840.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what about the reason I was asking you all these questions, Witness? The reason is this: I want to confront you with my theory. It would be entirely erroneous to believe that persons of Afro-Asian descent who came there to fight were a unified group, would it not?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would be entirely erroneous to believe that. They were not united. There were a lot of splinter groups, independent groups, who acted and fought on their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Likewise, it would be erroneous to believe that they were operating under a single command, would it not?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are entirely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Further, it would be very erroneous to believe, would it not, that all those who came to Central Bosnia from Afro-Asian countries during the war joined the El Mujahedin Detachment and were its members; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. There may have been more Arabs outside the detachment than in it, than Arabs who were actually members of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to move on now in order to clarify some parts of your statement in which you talked about the activities of some other Arab groups that were not part of the El Mujahedin Detachment. I mean their activities in Central Bosnia. Let me remind you that in paragraph 38 of your statement, you stated that the El Mujahedin Detachment, in October 1993, which is when you joined the detachment, had a total of three camps, Poljanica, Orasac and Vatrostalna at Zenica; is that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I joined in October 1993, and those were the three camps, the three barracks that the El Mujahedin Detachment had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. So what you know for sure is that the detachment had no other camps aside from these, did it?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this with sure and certain knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you explain what you mean by "with sure and certain knowledge"? Are you saying -- when you say you know this with sure and certain knowledge, are you suggesting there could be others outside your knowledge or you're saying you don't discount that possibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure I understand the interpreter. Can this be told me once again, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say you know this with sure and certain knowledge, is there something else you know without certain and -- without sure and certain knowledge, in relation to the question of camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say I know this for sure, I mean I can rule out the possibility that any other camp belonging to the El Mujahid Detachment existed at the time. That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The groups in the following camps, Gluha Bukovica near Travnik, did not in fact belong to the El Mujahedin Detachment, did they?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the group at Gluha Bukovica near Travnik did not belong to the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about the group at Guca Gora near Travnik; they were not part of the detachment, were they?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not part of the detachment either, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about the group at Bistricak near Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The group at Bistricak and their training camp were not part of the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about the group at Zeljezno Polje near Zepce?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No part of the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about the groups at Tesanj?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those neither.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Kalesija?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't even aware of that group myself. I wasn't aware of its existence, and needless to say it wasn't part of the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about the group near Konjic?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a part of the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
