utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Is my understanding correct, you were aware of all these groups, apart from the one at Kalesija; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of all the other ones, with the exception of that group you refer to as being based at or near Kalesija, but none of those groups were part of the El Mujahid Detachment. I was in fact aware the existence of some other groups which you have so far failed to mention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you give us a hand with that perhaps? Which groups are you thinking of?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the group of Turks who were known as "the Gerila group," and they were based in Zenica. They are the first to spring to mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I had totally forgotten about those. Witness, all these groups that we've enumerated were involved in the fighting in 1994 and 1995, were they not?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, they were involved in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My question was: All these groups were involved in the fighting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You are certain, are you not, that none of those groups, in 1994 or 1995, were operating under the command of the El Mujahedin Detachment at all?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm entirely certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will now go back to parts of your statement, paragraphs 101 through 106. In your statement, in paragraph 101, you say: "I had heard of a man named Abu Zubejr for the first time late in 1994." You also say that his unit was based in Zeljezno Polje. You described it as an informal unit, almost illegal?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let us dwell on the person of Abu Zubeir for a while. Do you agree with me that a number of different Afro-Asians who were in Bosnia at the time were nicknamed "Abu Zubeir"?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right. There were even some ethnic Bosnians who were nicknamed "Abu Zubeir" as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before I show you any exhibits, I want to ask you this. I looked at your statement, and I drew the following inference: You personally had occasion to see Abu Zubeir? I'm talking about the Abu Zubeir who led the unit that was based at Zeljezno Polje. If your memory is still clear enough, can you first describe the physical appearance of this person? Was there anything particularly distinctive about his appearance?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was distinctive about him was his obesity. I think he weighed over 150 kilos. He was about 180 centimetres tall. He was swarthy, a complexion as Arabs sometimes are, he had a beard that was average, not particularly long for an Arab, but he was fat, in a way. They used to call him "Abu Zubeir, the fat one," or, "Abu Zubeir, the bear," for that reason, because of his fatness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. The next exhibit that I would like the witness to look at is Exhibit 342. Page 2 in both the English and the B/C/S, please. The top half of the page, please. Thank you. In the English, it's the third paragraph: "Like Abu Sulaiman ...," that's how it begins.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I will now read to you the first two sentences of this paragraph. It reads: "Like Abu Sulaiman, Abu Zubair al-Haili, also known as The Bear, a 300-pound monster of a man, had also first gained a reputation as a fearless and calculating military commander in Afghanistan before serving as an artillery expert with the Arab Mujahedin in Bosnia." Witness, all I'm interested in is this: Do you agree that the physical description perfectly fits the Abu Zubeir that you actually met at the time, who was the commander of the Arab group based at Zeljezno Polje?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, and "al-Haili" also fits. That's Abu Zubeir. He was from Hail [phoen], which is a town in the north of Saudi Arabia, and that's how he got the nickname.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We can put this document away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You say that he was also known as "The Bear"; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you. Could we please have Exhibit 783 next. Again, information by the Security Service Administration, and the date is the 21st of June, 1995. Information on the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please look at the beginning of paragraph 2, which states: "In the conversation between Ebu Ejub and Ebu Jetam, Ebu Ejub wants to know where Ebu Jetam is. He then informs him that he was in the Tuzla group, that their Emir was Habab, and that the Tuzla group belongs to Ebu Zubejr." Witness, you told us that Ebu Zubeir or Abu Zubeir had this group at Zeljezno Polje. Did you know at the time that he had groups in other areas across Bosnia and Herzegovina as well?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he had certain groups elsewhere. The one at Gluha Bukovica I think also belonged to Abu Zubeir. As for the group at Tuzla, I think this is a reference to the one that you earlier mentioned referred to as the "Kalesija group," but I didn't know that it existed. Abu Ejub is someone that I'm familiar with and I know that he was a member of Abu Zubeir's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If my understanding is correct, these groups had no point of contact with your detachment; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, no point of contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you were familiar with the Travnik area, weren't you? Will you please tell the Chamber, what is the distance between Gluha Luka [as interpreted] and Mehurici, for example?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 15 and 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what about the distance to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm looking now at paragraph 103 of your statement, where you say that the Abu Zubeir group had a very negative attitude towards the El Mujahid Detachment. Is that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this Abu Zubeir al-Halili was never a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was never a member of the detachment, and I think -- I'm practically sure that he never entered any of the barracks of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, just one intervention for the transcript. Page 60, line 10 and 11, I said -- the witness and I spoke about Gluha Bukovica, and the transcript states "Gluha Luka." This is important. There is a significant distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you understood that I was speaking about Gluha Bukovica?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, Gluha Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is a good time to go for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see I understand you before the interpretation. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, we stopped when we were discussing Abu Zubeir. I would now like to remind you about what you said in your statement. In paragraph 104 of your statement, you said that Arabs from Saudi Arabia did not like having an Algerian guy as the commander of the El Mujahid Detachment. Actually, I would like to make an introduction. I would like to deal now with the situation in the detachment itself and some disagreements which I believe happened within the detachment. You talked about this in paragraph 104 of your statement. You said that Arabs from Saudi Arabia did not like to have an Algerian as the commander of the detachment, and they did not like the Egyptian environment. And in connection with that, I would like to ask you: The Algerian is Abu Maali; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And am I correct in believing that at one point, within the El Mujahedin Detachment itself, there was some kind of disagreement and a number of the detachment members left and joined Abu Zubeir's group?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, that is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember when this happened?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my recollection, I think this was in the second half of 1994. I cannot be certain about the date. I think it was towards the end of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're not interested in any more details for now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. It's sufficient for now. What I would like to ask you about Al Zubeir is the following: Within the detachment itself, there were members who had that nickname or name, but none of them was Abu Zubeir al-Halili; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zubeir al-Halili was the one who was the leader of the group in Zeljezno Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Among the groups that we discussed, we mentioned the group in Guca Gora. Can the witness please look at D645, please. While the document is being prepared, Witness, I would like to ask you this: You already mentioned that there were more persons with the nickname "Abu Hamza," so I would like to discuss something with you that concerns one of those people. As you can see on the screen, again this is an act by the Security Service in Zenica of the 9th -- of the 5th of November, 1993 -- 1995. It's an information to the Command of the 3rd Corps. It's a small document, and it states that the 7th Corps reported an event that took place in Guca Gora, in which members of the El Mujahid Detachment participated, led by Mr. Abu Hamza. And then the bottom part of the document states that the El Mujahedin Detachment Command was informed that Mr. Abu Hamza was not a member of their unit and is not a member of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they state that for those reasons, "He is not under our jurisdiction," and the act is being sent for the review of the police in relation to Abu Hamza. What I would like to ask you is the following: I mentioned the group in Guca Gora, and you said that El Mujahedin did not have a group in Guca Gora. Do you know if the group in Guca Gora was led by Abu Hamza?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with the group in Guca Gora that was headed by Abu Hamza Tunisi, and they had nothing to do with El Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've already told us that the only group leader or the only one who had a prominent position in El Mujahedin was Abu Hamza. You said Muhadzir, I think.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Muhadzir, and that he was the head of the detachment's press centre. This is what I would like to ask you: Incidents in the Travnik region were created by Abu Hamza Tunisi and this group from Guca Gora, not by members of the El Mujahedin Detachment, in the course of 1994 and 1995; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This Abu Hamza that is mentioned in this document was not a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, do you agree that local Bosnians who were not familiar with the structure of the detachment or of the Arabs felt that it was the simplest thing to connect incidents with El Mujahedin, which was the only body that they had any contact with; would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is something that happened all the time. People were not familiar with the fact that there were different groups and the relationships between them, so it was very simple to say, for any of them, that this was an Arab from the El Mujahedin Detachment, when actually it was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 841.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to show the witness another document. It's a photograph. Can we put this document away, and I would like the witness to look at Exhibit 92. 92, page 15. Could we please zoom in on the photograph. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to look at this photograph. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who this person is?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Imad Del Husen [phoen], known as Abu Hamza Suri.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If somebody were to link in any way this person with Abu Hamza from Guca Gora and the -- who created incidents, and as you have just said, they would very much be mistaken, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, because that is not the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, this photograph has already been given a number, and we don't need it anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just ask, did this Abu Hamza Suri belong to the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he was a member of the detachment. He joined the detachment in spring 1995, sometime in March or April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be put away now, and we would like the witness to look at Exhibit 345 now, please. Can we zoom in on this photograph. Otherwise, I will just ask the witness to look at the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I don't know if you can recognise the face. If you cannot, I'm going to give you a hard copy which we can place on the ELMO, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already seen this before in newspapers, so I am familiar with what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, this is a page from "Oslobodjenje." The article is "Zuhair, the real Handala."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the date of the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, did you see this article before, or this person in newspapers, this person Zuhair or Handala? Was he ever a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahmed Zuhair, known as Abu Handala, was never a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Furthermore, from what I know, he was not a member of the other units, either. He had a separate group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. We can put this document away now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us a bit earlier that locals could not differentiate among all these Arab groups, they were not aware of their existence. El Mujahid did have some connections with the army and he was known. You also told us that incidents were ascribed to the detachment for those reasons. I would like you to look at Exhibit 641 now, please. Witness, it's very hard to read this document, but I'm not interested in this page. I'm just going to tell you -- actually, perhaps the witness can look at the hard copy, Your Honours. The document is already exhibited. It is -- these are minutes from a meeting from the 2nd of September, 1995, in the Public Security Centre in Zenica. Representatives of the police are mentioned here. Can the witness please look at page 3 of the document. It's much more legible, and it's relevant for us. In the English version, also it is page 3. Witness, I would like to ask you to read paragraph 5, where it says: "Item 5", and I'm going to put some questions to you about that.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This document shows, does it not, that members from the government or authority noted that it was arbitrarily concluded that those who caused the incidents were from the El Mujahedin Detachment and that also these incidents were being ascribed to the detachment arbitrarily? Please, you, in the detachment, were you aware of this situation? Was it known in the detachment that incidents were being ascribed to the members of the detachment? And if you were, what happened in that case?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that many incidents were ascribed to the detachment for which the detachment members were not responsible. As for what was specifically done, I don't know. I know that the detachment command tried to clarify the situation, and I know that they even assisted the Military Police of the 3rd Corps in arresting some people who were of Afro-Asian extraction, who had been responsible for causing disturbances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would like you to comment on this part here, where it says it is necessary to identify the perpetrators of incidents, and it says this is necessary in order to get rid of insinuations spread by malicious persons that all of those who caused the incidents were from the El Mujahedin Detachment. Is it true that this was something -- a story that was being spread maliciously?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was my impression at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you this: It's correct, isn't it, that in Central Bosnia, in particular, many humanitarian organisations were active from the Arab world?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is also correct, isn't it, that they also embarked on combat actions?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they also went into combat action. I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What is correct is that they did not join members of detachments, they did not enter combat actions under the command of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No humanitarian organisation participated in combat actions together with the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now going to put some questions to you relating to your testimony on the detachment itself and on the structure of the El Mujahedin Detachment, because I think that you can shed some light on these questions. In paragraph 33 of the statement, you said that Dr. Abu Haris Al-Libi was the detachment commander?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Abu Haris Al-Libi was the detachment commander until December 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. He graduated at the Faculty of Medicine, and before the war he worked as a doctor in Austria; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The military commander, Muatez whom you mentioned, before the war was a lawyer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 33 of the statement, you said that the El Mujahedin Detachment had a specific structure. You said that it was officially registered in the 3rd Corps. Then you said that it should have had the structure of an anti-sabotage detachment. And then you said that that was the structure only on paper. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By establishment, the way it was supposed to be, according to the army rules, the detachment, the Anti-Sabotage Detachment, should have consisted of three companies, as I explained that in my statement, but the El Mujahedin Detachment actually functioned according to some quite different principles and according to a different organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to come to that, but before that, I would like you to look at Exhibit 273. It's an order from the Supreme Command Staff of the 13th of August, 1993, founding the El Mujahedin Detachment once the -- and it was formed in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. I'm going to ask you to look at this part here that has to do with mobilisation preparation. I'm going to quote. It says in the document: "Replenish the El Mujahedin Detachment with foreign volunteers currently on the territory of the 3rd Corps area of responsibility." I know that you were not a member of the detachment when this order was issued, but I would like to ask you this: When you came to the detachment, you found a situation whereby the detachment did not consist of only foreigners, but it included at least half or maybe more of local fighters?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The entire time that the detachment existed, the bulk of its forces were locals, Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You will agree with me, will you not, that this order, immediately after it was issued, was not actually respected, it did not provide for something like that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen this order before, and it envisaged that the detachment be formed out of foreigners. But, however, from Day 1 this order was not actually followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you about another aspect of this document. It also says here that it should be formed with foreign volunteers currently on the territory of the 3rd Corps area of responsibility. What I would like to ask you is this: It's correct, isn't it, that foreigners, many foreigners who happened to be in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps at the time, never actually joined the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpretation that I heard and as it appears on the transcript says: "It also says here that it should be formed with foreign volunteers." Now, the order says "Replenish" in the English. What does the B/C/S say, sir? Can you read for us? Does the -- if you can just read that paragraph immediately under the heading "Formation."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I made a mistake. It does say "popunu," "replenish," "to replenish," as you have read from the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I would just like to clarify something in relation to this. So you understood that -- well, let me ask you this: Is there a difference, linguistically, between "to form from" and "replenish"? If you believe that there is a difference, maybe I can put the question to you again.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is no difference. This is classic military terminology, to replenish and to form, whatever is used in this case means the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just something else. In other words, the detachment was not replenished only by foreigners but also by locals; that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, can this document now be -- just one thing before we put the document away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, please, you would agree, would you not, that in this last sentence on this page, it says these people should keep the weapons and other equipment which has already been issued to them? Would you agree that -- or, actually, do you have any information about where these weapons came from that members of the detachment had? Did they receive these weapons from the army or did they already have these weapons? Did they buy them with their own funds?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole time that I was in the detachment, the detachment dealt, itself, with the issue of materiel and logistics by purchasing this stuff. They did not have any assistance from the army, and it was not issued to them from the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You had the opportunity to discuss this with people from the detachment, with other members of the detachment. Did anybody ever tell you that the army, in 1993, issued weapons to them?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of anyone being issued weapons from the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Maybe now we can put this document away. Your Honours, can we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I'll be asking you to look at another document produced by the Military Security Service Administration, 3rd Corps, Zenica, the 19th of December, 1995. Again -- can the document please be shown in such a way that the witness can see the entire page. Can you please read to yourself what it says? And this is page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you scroll up in the English, please. It doesn't look like the beginning of the sentence. Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us as soon as you're done so we can move on to the next page, Witness? Can you just focus on the word "Keteba" [phoen] written here, "Kataabo," "Keteba"?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, while we're still looking at this page, let me ask you this: Do you agree that the document reflects the atmosphere of this newly-arisen situation after the signing of the peace agreement in Paris, and this reflects on the detachment; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It talks about dissatisfaction because of the fact that the detachment is to be dismantled and they are being ordered to leave the country; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Dissatisfaction at the move of the Bosnian government because the Bosnian government agreed to this peace agreement; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Now, there's this reference to this word "Keteba." In the brackets, it reads that this is most probably the name of an organisation, El Keteba, that is Arabic for the "El Mujahedin Detachment"; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Keteba" means "detachment" in the Arabic language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is quite obvious that the Bosnian Security Services themselves knew very little about the detachment. They didn't even know that Keteba was a detachment; they thought this was some sort of organisation or something?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe that what they knew was precious little.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please go to page 2 of this document. It's page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we pull the page up a little, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'll be asking you to pay close attention to the paragraph midway down the page. Your Honours, it's the part which in English begins with the word "Furthermore." Witness, let us try to save time. I quote: "Furthermore, it is suggested that the Mujahedins should wait for a day or two to see how the situation would develop, because concerning their case, the Shura, Keteba holds a session every 15 minutes. This shows clearly that the Shura continued to operate and exist until the detachment was dismantled; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the Shura that took the decision to -- for the El Mujahedin Detachment to cease to exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, could we please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 843.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me remind you of another section of your statement. In your evidence today, you mentioned Sheik Enver, his death, and you said that he was a member of the detachment's command, which is something that I wish to clarify. The page I invoke here is page 5, lines 2 and 3, I believe. I think that was the page being shown at the moment. Be that as it may, Witness, can we please look into the role of Sheik Enver. In paragraphs 160 through 164 of your statement, you say, about Sheik Saban: "Sheik Anwar Saban was the political authority of the El Mujahid Detachment. As far as I know, he came from Italy right before our second operation at Teslic." And then you go on to state, and I'm quoting your words from paragraph 164: "Officially, Sheik Anwar did not perform any function in the El Mujahedin Detachment, but in fact he was very influential. Muatez, Abu Maali and others respected and obeyed him very much." And now I'm thinking of what you said today, that he was a member of the detachment's command, and that strikes me as being different from what you stated in your original statement. Can you please shed some light on the actual role played by Sheik Saban?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't literally remember what I said, but I thought that Sheik Enver Saban was a member of the detachment's leadership. It might be a rather demanding exercise and I might take up some more time, trying to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please, by all means do so.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, basically, the El Mujahid Detachment was a part of the Dzemat, it was part of a community that had its political objectives and other kinds of objectives, too. The principal objective of this Dzemat was Dawa, which is what we spoke about a while ago, missionary work, work on promoting Islamic values, principles and the like. It was within the framework of that Dzemat, of that community, that the El Mujahid Detachment came into existence, as well as a number of other institutions and humanitarian organisations, such as the Institution for Missionary Work and the like. It was the Shura that was at the head of this all. It was the highest-ranking body, the supreme body. In formal terms, it was above Sheik Enver Saban. But I don't think any decision could have been taken by the Shura that would have strayed from any preferences expressed by the sheik. In a way, what that means is that he was the number-one man, and that is why I said originally that he was not a member of the detachment's command. This was a broader institution than the Command itself, and the institution that I have in mind is the Dzemat, the community.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You talked about him being a political sort of authority; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I think that is the aptest possible explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Could the witness now be shown D624.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, can I just ask, what is a Dzemat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Dzemat" verbatim, in Arabic, means "community." This would imply that this is an organisation that is independent, an organisation that has certain political objectives and other objectives independently of anyone else. It has its own hierarchy, its own structure. It has a Shura, it has an emir, it has a Dzemat, it has its own institutions which it uses to further its own objectives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How big is it, in terms of membership?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no rule. It can be anything from five persons up. There is no rule that defines this. Specifically, if we look at the Dzemat of the Mujahedin in Bosnia, it had a lot of members, all the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment plus a number of others who were not members of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we have a look at D624. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the witness -- or before the document appears on our screens:

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Members of these other groups, such as, for example, Abu Zubeir, were they members of the Dzemat?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not members of the Dzemat. When I spoke about members who were not part of the El Mujahedin Detachment, those were people who were in charge of our finances, for example, collecting donations, funding, that sort of thing, general support being provided for the work of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like you to focus on this document that is before us. What about the person you see in this photograph? Can we please zoom in slightly, if possible, on the photograph. I believe you see the Bosnian. The person shown in the photograph, is this Sheik Enver Saban?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now for the text, please. Page 2 of the document. The English is all right. In Bosnian, this is page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You realise that this article was published in "The Lily" on the 15th of November, 1995. Could we just see the heading, please. The first caption, can you see that? I need a small portion of the article which I want the witness to look at. Just under the heading, there is a portion of the text where we see the Sheik introduce himself. He talks about missionary work performed in the service of Islam, about the Islamic political movements. Can you just focus on the portion which says: "Interviewed by Nedzid Latic," and the question is: "Is your real name Sheik Enver?" And then he says: "My real name is Sheik Enver Saban." Question: "Where were you born? Answer: "In Egypt." Question: "What is your profession?" Answer: "I am a diar [phoen], a missionary." Question: "Which schools did you complete?" Answer: "I graduated from the Faculty of the Technical Sciences in Cairo." So this is Sheik Enver Saban, the person you discussed?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sheik Enver Saban actually used his real name in Bosnia, didn't he? He did not try to conceal his real identity. This is an article published during the war.

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Day 1 Sheik Enver Saban never tried to conceal his identity. It would have been always an uphill struggle for him. He had been the director of the Islamic Institute in Milan, Italy, and from Day 1 he was known to all and sundry as "Sheik Enver Saban."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us that Sheik Enver was some sort of a political player, and now you said that he had previously worked as director of the Islamic Institute in Milan, Italy. Would it be accurate to say that Sheik Enver was the ideological and political leader whom the detachment commanders followed?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is an accurate statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: He was the real authority for the commanders of the detachment; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the real authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Chamber what the word "fatwa" means, "fatwa"?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hear you loud and clear. I'm thinking, because I'm trying to explain in the briefest possible terms. "Fatwa" would be an interpretation preferred by certain Islamic authority, an interpretation of an Islamic prescription or rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who would have been authorised to pronounce a fatwa?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are certain broad rules covering this. We'll not need to go into that now. But the sheik's students, in terms of Islamic teaching, are authorised to pronounce fatwas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You agree that the sheik, Sheik Enver in this case, in exercising his authority for as long as he was in Bosnia, pronounced fatwas?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is something about the transcript. Your Honours, page 90, line 4, the witness said "learned men," "ucenjaci" and what we see in the transcript is "students," "ucenici," and these are two very different words. "Ucenjaci" and "ucenici," two very different words.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think the interpreter got it the other way around, it's "learned men" and not "students."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So "learned men," that's what you were trying to say?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now let me go back to the fatwa. You told us that Sheik Enver pronounced fatwas. Am I right in saying that this is a binding decision?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was binding for the detachment. It needn't have been binding for anyone who was outside that particular dzemat. If they decided to follow of their own accord, well, that was their own business.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But for the detachment itself, it would have been binding, would it not?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What sort of fatwas were these being pronounced by Sheik Enver? Do you remember any specific ones?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd need to have a think, really, to recall a particular one. There is one that I remember. All right. The war was nearing its end, and people were saying that there would be an election soon after the war, so he pronounced a fatwa that none of the members of the Dzemat would take part in those elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. I'm not sure if my understanding is correct. This is a very impressive example that you've just provided. In other words, if such a fatwa is pronounced, even if it is contrary to the position that the state itself takes, or a state authority, facing a situation like that, what would the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment do? Would they follow the instructions of the state authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina or would they obey the fatwa?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said already, Sheik Enver's fatwas were binding for the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment, and his authority was never questioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Before we wrap up for the day, I have one or two questions. In your statement, you say that Sheik Enver arrived in Bosnia before the second Seric battle; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Meaning autumn 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The operation occurred on the 3rd of October [Realtime transcript read in error "November"]. He had arrived just prior to that. I can't say exactly how long before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Were someone to say that Sheik Enver, under his real name or an assumed false name, was the Commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment from October 1992 and onwards, that would not be an accurate statement, would it?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not. Sheik Enver arrived in the autumn of 1994. He had not been in the country up until then. In October 1992, there was no such thing as the El Mujahedin Detachment, so how could he have possibly been its commander?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I don't think the interpretation is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, can you please repeat what you just said, the last sentence? You said, "In October 1992 --"

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such thing as the El Mujahedin Detachment, so how could anyone have been its member, Sheik Enver or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, here we see the word "commander" instead of [indiscernible] ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And now let me ask you this: Were someone to say that Sheik Enver was a member of the BH Army throughout that time, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: PW-9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Sheik Enver was never a member of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. Your Honours, could we please have an exhibit -- I think that this is it for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 844.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, before we go for the day, sir, I would like you to just tell us what you say a fatwa is. You said "fatwa" would be an interpretation preferred by certain Islamic authority, an interpretation of an Islamic prescription or rule. Then when you said a fatwa can be given to say people must not vote in elections, that seems to me like a fatwa is an order. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be interpreted as an order. However, an order based on an Islamic rule or prescription. Sheik Enver's interpretation in this specific case would be that this was a non-Islamic principle, in terms of electing a state leadership, and that was why he said that no members should be involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In any case, they were not citizens of Bosnia, so they couldn't vote in any case, even without the fatwa; am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But most of the members of the detachment and the Dzemat were Bosnians, such as me and hundreds of others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you vote?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not at those elections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll adjourn to tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this court. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 16th day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
